record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: For the radial solutions of problem (II) on Ω = B_r(0), where the cited work finds two radial solutions for λ* < λ < λ** and only the upper branch for λ > λ**, what mechanism explains why the lower radial branch stops at λ = λ** when the branch otherwise stays inside the positive cone and reaches zero normal derivative there?

evidence.quote: there are two radial solutions u1 and u2 verifying u1 < u2 and for λ > λ** there is only the solution u2.
Here we have a complete description of radial solutions, and we may ask why the branch "stops" at the value λ = λ**.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Ω = B_r(0) ⊂ ℝ^N be the open ball of radius r > 0 centered at the origin, and fix a constant β ∈ (0,1). Consider the singular semilinear elliptic problem with absorption

(II)    −Δu + u^{−β} χ_{{u>0}} = λ g(u) in Ω,    u ≥ 0 in Ω,    u = 0 on ∂Ω,

where λ > 0 is a real parameter and g : [0,∞) → [0,∞) is a fixed continuous nonlinearity (for instance g(s) = s^q with q ∈ (0,1) or another sublinear/superlinear model giving the bifurcation diagram described below). A solution u to (II) is called a free-boundary solution if the set {u = 0} ∩ Ω has nonempty interior and on its boundary one has u = 0 and ∇u = 0 simultaneously; otherwise u is called strictly positive (lying in the positive cone, with u > 0 in Ω).

Assume that the radial bifurcation diagram of (II) has the following structure: there exist 0 < λ_* < λ_{**} < ∞ such that
(a) for every λ ∈ (λ_*, λ_{**}) there exist exactly two radial solutions u_1(·;λ) < u_2(·;λ) of (II), both strictly positive in Ω;
(b) for every λ > λ_{**} only the upper radial solution u_2(·;λ) exists;
(c) as λ ↑ λ_{**}, the lower radial branch u_1(·;λ) remains strictly positive inside Ω and converges to a limit profile u_1(·;λ_{**}) which still satisfies u_1 > 0 in Ω, vanishes on ∂Ω, and has zero normal derivative on ∂Ω, i.e. ∂u_1/∂ν = 0 on ∂Ω.

Question. Determine and rigorously justify the analytic/geometric mechanism that forces the lower radial branch λ ↦ u_1(·;λ) to terminate exactly at λ = λ_{**}: that is, explain why this branch cannot be continued to values λ > λ_{**} even though, at λ = λ_{**}, u_1 still belongs to the positive cone and only meets the boundary tangentially (with simultaneous vanishing of u and of ∂u/∂ν on ∂Ω).
artifact.status_search_result: The overview where this question is posed explicitly raises it as an open problem ("we may ask why the branch stops at the value λ = λ**"). Subsequent literature on singular semilinear/quasilinear elliptic problems with absorption and free boundary (Díaz–Hernández and coauthors, and follow-up works such as the 2023 study of −Δu = λu − u^{−1} with Neumann data) discusses bifurcation diagrams with multiple radial branches, but no published result was found that rigorously identifies the precise mechanism causing the lower radial branch in problem (II) on a ball to terminate at λ**. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Positive and Free Boundary Solutions to Singular Nonlinear Elliptic Problems with Absorption: An Overview and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of existence and multiplicity of positive and/or compact support solutions to semilinear elliptic equations with singular absorption nonlinearities, listing open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly posed as an open problem in this survey.

status_evidence.title: Branches of positive and free boundary solutions for some singular quasilinear elliptic problems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies existence and multiplicity of strictly positive and free-boundary solutions for one-dimensional quasilinear singular eigenvalue problems, exhibiting bifurcation branches.
status_evidence.claim: Related work characterizing bifurcation branches but not resolving the termination mechanism for the multidimensional radial problem (II).

status_evidence.title: Radial Solutions and a Local Bifurcation Result for a Singular Elliptic Problem with Neumann Condition
status_evidence.snippet: Bifurcation analysis for −Δu = λu − u^{−1} with Neumann data; proves global character of one bifurcation branch in the radial case.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on related singular bifurcation problems; does not resolve the cited termination question for problem (II).
